body:
### Description

Once a session holds more than 25 MiB of inline images, `boundImages` in `packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts` replaces the oldest images with a text note until the rest fits in 15 MiB. It recomputes this on every request, so each new image moves the cutoff and changes the history near the start. Anthropic caches by prefix, so from then on every turn writes the whole context to cache again.

I hit this with two Claude subagents that read a lot of screenshots. After the trim kicked in, cache reads stayed at the system prompt size (about 15k tokens) and every turn wrote 150k to 200k tokens to cache. Those turns cost $49 of one run's $57 and $54 of the other's $59.

### OpenCode version

v2.0.18

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an Anthropic model.
2. Read screenshots with the `read` tool until the session holds more than 25 MiB of images.
3. Keep reading images. Each turn reports a cache read the size of the system prompt and a cache write the size of the full context.

### Operating System

macOS

I have a fix ready and will open a PR.

comments.body:
This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- [#48095](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/48095): Proposes an in-memory rolling window that replaces older images during context assembly.
- [#43722](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/43722): Reports prompt-cache misses caused by rewriting model-visible history.

title: Image trimming breaks Anthropic prompt caching on every turn
